title: NonnegativeSmoothSampleLoss.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective is the population loss f(x) = E[ℓω(x)] on a second-countable real Hilbert space. Both the sample losses and their expectation may be nonconvex. The public inputs include the initial point x₀, the common smoothness bound L > 0, the bound Δ ≥ 0 on f(x₀), and the target ε > 0.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NonnegativeSmoothSampleLoss.lean, Params and spec.{Public, publicInput, valid, admissible}

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: One call at (x,y) returns (∇ℓω(x), ∇ℓω(y)) for the same hidden sample ω. Calls use independent draws from a common hidden law. The reply contains only the two gradients, and the cost counts each pair as one call.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Every sample loss is globally nonnegative and has an L-Lipschitz gradient. These assumptions imply ‖∇ℓω(x)‖² ≤ 2Lℓω(x), so the gradient second moment is bounded by 2Lf(x) at each x and by 2LΔ at initialization. This bound can grow with the objective value. Individual samples may have different minimizers.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/NonnegativeSmoothSampleLoss.lean, spec.admissible, clauses for nonnegativity, HasGradientAt, the sample-gradient Lipschitz bound, the expectation defining f, and f(x₀) ≤ Δ

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns a measurable point X in the Hilbert space. Its population-gradient norm must be integrable and satisfy E[‖∇f(X)‖] ≤ ε.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The expectation averages over both the algorithm seed and the independent oracle sample stream under a fixed cap on paired calls.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation combines same-sample gradient pairs with a loss-dependent noise bound derived from sample nonnegativity and smoothness. The public initial-loss bound controls the initial noise scale while allowing variance to grow elsewhere.

descriptionHtml:
Stationarity for Nonnegative Smooth Sample Losses

We consider minimizing a possibly nonconvex expected loss f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space E. Every sample loss is nonnegative and has an L-Lipschitz gradient, where L>0. A given starting point x0∈E satisfies f(x0)≤Δ for a bound Δ≥0. Each oracle call returns the sample gradients at two queried points using a single fresh independent sample. For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E satisfying E[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε, with expectation over the algorithm and oracle randomness.

Let (Ω,F) be the sample space, p a probability law on it, and ℓ(x,ω) the loss at x∈E for sample ω∈Ω. The optimization problem is infx∈Ef(x),f(x)=Eω∼p[ℓ(x,ω)]. The algorithm receives E with its Borel structure, (Ω,F), x0, L, Δ, and ε.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Sample losses). For every x∈E, the function ℓ(x,⋅) is p-integrable. For every ω∈Ω, the function ℓ(⋅,ω) is differentiable on E. Its gradient g(x,ω)=∇xℓ(x,ω) is jointly measurable in (x,ω). For all x,y∈E and ω∈Ω, ℓ(x,ω)≥0,∥g(x,ω)−g(y,ω)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Paired gradient queries). The oracle samples (ξk)k≥0 are independent random variables with common law p. The sample sequence is independent of the algorithm’s randomness. On call k, a query (x,y)∈E×E receives the reply (g(x,ξk),g(y,ξk)).

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable, its gradient norm must be integrable, and E[∥∇f(x¯)∥]≤ε.

theorems.formulaHtml: ⌈8192⋅(1+L⋅Δε2)3⌉+

comparisonHtml:
On a separable real Hilbert space, F(x)=Eξℓξ(x) with ℓξ(x)≥0 integrable for each x. Sample gradients are jointly measurable and L-Lipschitz in x for every sample, with L>0 and F(x0)≤Δ. Each pair call evaluates two gradients at queried points using one fresh IID sample. The target is a measurable X with E∥∇F(X)∥≤ε, ε>0.

Sufficient oracle budgets for expected stationarity with nonnegative smooth sample losses.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) NonnegativeSampleStationarity (Ours) (review) O(1+(LΔ/ε2)3/2) pair calls, including the initial batch.
(2) Normalized STORM (auto-math-bot 2026) O(1+(LΔ/ε2)3/2) pair calls on the shared class. (1): Matches the known rate and tuning. The sample-level formalization derives E∥∇ℓξ(x)∥2≤2LF(x). (1) requires nonnegative smooth losses. (2) allows mean-square smooth gradients with variance bounded by an affine function of the objective gap.
(3) SGD (Khaled and Richtárik 2020, Cor. 1) O(1+(LΔ/ε2)2) single gradients. Derived bound. (1): For R≥1, the gradient budget improves by a factor of order R, as in (2). For R≤1, the orders match. (1) needs same-sample pairs. (3) queries one point per sample and bounds the minimum expected squared gradient norm across iterates.
(4) SPIDER (Chen et al. 2023, Thm. 4) O(R(1+Γ2)+Λ2/ε2+R(1+Γ)Λ/ε) gradient evaluations. Derived bound for small ε at fixed parameters, LΔ>0. (1) covers samples violating the affine variance bound required by (4). On the overlap, its ε−3 coefficient is smaller when (1+Γ)Λ≫LΔ. (1) requires nonnegative smooth losses even on affine-variance problems. On the overlap its leading term is worse when (1+Γ)Λ≪LΔ; at Λ=0, (4) needs O(R(1+Γ2)).

Abbr: R=LΔ/ε2. The affine variance parameters Γ,Λ≥0 satisfy E∥∇ℓξ(x)−∇F(x)∥2≤Γ2∥∇F(x)∥2+Λ2.

import LongTails.Setups.ExpectedSmoothnessNonconvex

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.NonnegativeSmoothSampleLoss

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  x0 : E
  L : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.completeE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.countableE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := q.E → ℝ
  Query q := q.E × q.E
  Reply q := q.E × q.E
  Output q := q.E
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (loss : q.Ω → q.E → ℝ) (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E)
      (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
      StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω, law := P, answer := fun _ (_, xy) ω => (g xy.1 ω, g xy.2 ω) } ∧
      (∀ ω x, 0 ≤ loss ω x) ∧ (∀ ω x, HasGradientAt (loss ω) (g x ω) x) ∧
      (∀ ω x y, ‖g x ω - g y ω‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧ (∀ x, Integrable (fun ω => loss ω x) (p : Measure _)) ∧
      (∀ x, f x = ∫ ω, loss ω x ∂(p : Measure _)) ∧ f q.x0 ≤ q.Δ
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.NonnegativeSmoothSampleLoss
